title: Exact Neural-Network Representations of the Motzkin States
authors: Runde Zha, Yuntian Gu, Chaohui Fan, Jia-lin Chen, Hai-Jun Liao, Tao Xiang
abstract: Motzkin spin chains are paradigmatic frustration-free one-dimensional quantum systems whose ground states feature exactly solvable combinatorial structures and exotic, area-law-violating entanglement scaling. Specifically, colorless Motzkin states exhibit critical logarithmic entanglement divergence \(\log N\) with system size \(N\), while their colorful counterparts host supercritical sublinear \(\sqrt{N}\) entanglement growth. Such unconventional entanglement behaviors place these states well beyond the expressive capability of standard matrix product states, which are fundamentally constrained by the entanglement area law. Here, we systematically construct exact, training-free neural-network representations for both colorless and colorful Motzkin states across four mainstream architectures, including recurrent, feedforward, convolutional, and transformer networks. Our core design leverages a causal prefix-sum module, implementable via recurrent updates, feedforward mappings, or masked attention layers, combined with position-selective rectified linear gates that enforce the Motzkin height constraints. For the colorful states, we further introduce a dedicated causal stack module that explicitly encodes the last-in-first-out color-matching rule. Our results demonstrate that neural architectures can accurately capture highly non-trivial entanglement features inaccessible to conventional tensor networks, providing prototypic examples for benchmarking and a constructive design framework for future neural-network quantum state developments targeting strongly entangled quantum systems.
summary: This paper develops analytic, fixed-weight neural network representations for Motzkin spin chains, which are known to exhibit entanglement scaling beyond the area law. By adapting recurrent, convolutional, and transformer architectures, the authors prove that NNs can faithfully encode these complex combinatorial constraints. This establishes a general design principle for using neural networks as powerful tools to model strongly entangled quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The core problem is constructing exact, training-free neural network representations for Motzkin states whose entanglement properties exceed those captured by standard Matrix Product States.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated that multiple neural architectures (RNN, FNN, CNN, Transformer) can analytically encode the complex support of these highly entangled quantum states.
method: They systematically designed fixed-weight NQS layers incorporating causal prefix-sum modules and specialized gates to enforce combinatorial path constraints (height matching and color matching).
model_or_system: The system studied is the Motzkin spin chain, which includes colorless generalizations defined by height constraints and colorful versions requiring an additional last-in-first-out color-matching rule.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy scaling ($\log N$ for colorless; $\sqrt{N}$ for colorful), and the ability to reproduce the exact support of the ground state wavefunction.
important_parameters: System size $N$, and the specific architectural components (e.g., causal prefix-sum module, color stack).
main_assumptions: The representations are fixed-weight constructions based on the assumption that the state's support is governed by a finite causal algorithm.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Motzkin path constraints, including height violations and legal/illegal color matching paths for small system sizes ($N=4$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical properties and entanglement scaling of Motzkin states based on their Hamiltonian. It then systematically details how four different neural network architectures (RNN, FNN, CNN, Transformer) can mathematically reproduce the exact support required by these path constraints.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, constructive framework showing that advanced NNs can encode quantum correlations beyond simple area-law scaling, offering new benchmarks for simulating strongly correlated systems where standard tensor networks fail.
